data.title: Treasure Trove Assembles the “Avengers of Collectibles” as Advisory Board
data.description:
Treasure Trove Assembles the “Avengers of Collectibles” as Advisory Board

Four of the most influential figures in collectibles back AJ Scaramucci's collectibles holding company as advisors, bringing institutional rigor to a multi-trillion-dollar asset class

Treasure Trove, the collectibles holding company building the "Cultural Store of Value," today announced an advisory board that reads like an all-star roster of the industry: Ken Goldin, founder of Goldin; Jeremy Padawer, lifelong collector and investor; and Jim Halperin and Steve Ivy, co-founders of Heritage Auctions.

"This is the Avengers of the collectibles world," said AJ Scaramucci, founder of Treasure Trove. "These are the people who built this industry. Having them on board — with their own capital at stake — is a validation of the thesis we've been building: that grail-level collectibles are a serious, investable asset class."

The board brings deep, complementary expertise across every major collectibles category. Jim Halperin and Steve Ivy built Heritage Auctions into one of the largest auction houses in the world — spanning pop culture, movie props, comics, coins, and trading cards — and are on pace to break their own annual gross-sales record for the sixth consecutive year. Ken Goldin, founder of Goldin and known as "the King of Collectibles," has sold billions of dollars of collectibles throughout his career. With deep expertise in sports cards and memorabilia, he worked with Treasure Trove on its record-setting Joe Montana jersey acquisition. Jeremy Padawer, a center node in the collector economy, is a true collectibles investor who runs his own underwriting model and identified Pokémon cards as a serious investment opportunity in 2018, watching select assets appreciate roughly one hundredfold in the years that followed.

Beyond credibility, the board delivers what the company describes as its single biggest operational advantage: collectively, the advisors know where grail-level assets are held and who owns them — an edge that is difficult to replicate and one that is central to Treasure Trove's acquisition strategy.

"Collectibles have evolved from passion assets into a serious global asset class, and Treasure Trove is building for what comes next," said Padawer. "I'm excited to join the advisory board and help identify, acquire, steward, and tell the stories of the world's most iconic cultural assets with the discipline, ambition and long-term vision they deserve."

Why Collectibles, and Why Now

Treasure Trove frames collectibles alongside gold and Bitcoin as a third category of scarce, store-of-value assets — first was physical, then digital, and now cultural. As currencies continue to debase and AI drives the cost of intelligence toward zero, capital will increasingly flow into these kinds of scarce assets. The company applies the same underwriting discipline to acquiring one-of-one "grail" assets that an investor would apply to securities or companies, targeting pieces with a history of compounding faster than market rates of return.

The numbers increasingly bear that out: the legendary Babe Ruth Called Shot jersey compounded at a 19% IRR over nearly 20 years since its first official sale in 2005. Treasure Trove’s own Pikachu Illustrator has returned a 73% IRR since its first recorded sale in 2015, and its PSA 9.6 A++ copy of Super Mario Bros.—which Treasure Trove landed by outbidding Reddit co-founder and collectibles enthusiast Alexis Ohanian—has compounded 51% since a similar transaction in 2019. Countless examples show that top-tier assets across cards, comics, and memorabilia have posted returns that rival traditional financial markets and alternatives.

"The collectibles market has always been driven by passion, and that will never change," said Scaramucci. "What we're adding is institutional financial rigor, treating these assets with the seriousness they've always deserved. That expertise builds on a run of headline acquisitions, including the Montana jersey, the PSA 10 Pikachu Illustrator card acquired for approximately $16.5 million, and the first appearance of Iron Man (Tales of Suspense #39), a comic book from 1963 that is in perfect condition."

About Treasure Trove

Treasure Trove is a collectibles holding company building the Cultural Store of Value, acquiring one-of-one grail assets across categories including trading cards, comics, and sports memorabilia. Recent acquisitions include the PSA 10 Pikachu Illustrator card, the first appearance of Iron Man (Tales of Suspense #39), the highest-graded copy of the earliest sealed edition of Super Mario Bros, and Joe Montana's record-setting Super Bowl XXIV jersey. The company partners with museums to exhibit its holdings and produces short- and long-form media chronicling the history of iconic collectibles and the journeys behind acquiring them. Its podcast, Treasure Hunters, has featured guests such as Palmer Luckey, Logan Paul, and Benji and Joel Madden of Good Charlotte.

data.title: This investment is safe from both Trump and the Democrats - and it pays 4.7%
data.description:
By Brett Arends

There's a safe haven hiding in plain sight

Whatever happens, we'll have the best Congress money can buy.

If you're nervous, alarmed or hysterical about what's going on in Washington and on Wall Street right now, there is at least one safe haven you can buy today that is effectively guaranteed to ride out any storm. And it is currently paying 4.7% interest.

I'm talking about U.S. Treasury bonds - IOUs issued by Uncle Sam - that come due in early 2029, shortly after the (scheduled) end of the Trump administration.

No matter what happens in U.S. politics or finance, the chance that the U.S. government would default within the next three years is effectively nonexistent.

Famous last words? Even the gloomiest prognosticator doesn't see a fiscal crisis being realized in anything like that time frame.

Yet the panic about the budget, combined with panic about inflation and everything else, has driven the interest rate available on 3-year Treasury bonds to remarkably high levels.

The best rate available at the moment is on the Feb. 15, 2029 "zero-coupon" Treasury bonds (CUSIP: 912833XN5), which will pay you 4.7% a year between now and when it comes due. That will be less than a month after America gets a president who doesn't think the appropriate response to a war, $100-a-barrel oil (CL00) (BRN00) and a U.S. fiscal crisis involves renaming Lake Ontario, threatening Iceland or trying to bribe voters with $5,000 of their own money.

A zero-coupon Treasury bond can best be understood as one that doesn't pay interest as it goes along, but pays you the full amount - return of principal, plus all the accumulated interest - on the due date.

In this case, if you invest $1,000 in the bond, you will get back about $1,118 soon after President Vance, Rubio, Ocasio-Cortez, Beshear, Whitmer, MTG or Laura Loomer is sworn in.

Most of the time, you can sleep even easier if you buy inflation-protected Treasury bonds instead of regular Treasury bonds. These bonds, known as TIPS, use a complex system to ensure that you are compensated no matter what happens to consumer prices over the life of the bond. Right now, the April, 2029, 3.875% TIPS bond 912810FH69 will pay you 2.3% a year plus inflation over the life of the bond.

As inflation is currently running at over 3% a year, if this persists you'd earn 5.3% a year. Inflation would have to average less than 2.4% a year over the next two-and-a-half years for these bonds to work out worse than the regular 4.7% Treasurys mentioned above.

You can count me skeptical about that.

If you have a tax-sheltered account, such as an IRA, or a 401(k) that allows you to direct your own investments, that's the best place to hold taxable bonds such as Treasurys and TIPS. Bond interest is taxed federally at ordinary income-tax rates, which are usually higher than the tax rates on stock dividends and long-term capital gains.

At the moment, TIPS bonds pretty much across the board look like that extremely rare bird on Wall Street: a one-way bet. Those which come due within the next 10 years currently offer yields, or interest rates, of annual inflation plus up to 2.5% a year.

Even if you fall into the camp of those who think the U.S. fiscal crisis might end in outright default, you have to take a very extreme view to think that is likely to happen within the next 10 years. Even the April 2032, 3.375% TIPS bond 912810FQ68 is paying more than inflation plus 2.3% a year. How, exactly, would the U.S. default before 2032? (And, just as relevantly - even if that happened, what would happen to all your other investments?)

TIPS bonds that mature over 20 or even 30 years offer still better interest rates of up to 3.1% plus inflation per year. Such guaranteed rates are exceptionally rare by historical standards. (I've written about them before.)

Fears about U.S. budget deficits are rising, and these bonds may be subject to plenty of volatility. Bonds are like seesaws, so if the price falls, the yield rises. There is nothing to stop these bonds getting still cheaper in a panic about the U.S. Treasury market, and the yield rising still further.

But the only circumstance where they turn out to be a poor investment if you held them to maturity would be in the case of an actual U.S. government default. Those who think a default is a plausible outcome may be looking only at finances and forgetting the politics.

As we all know, the U.S. is an effective plutocracy. The richest 1% of families own about a third of all national wealth, and the richest 10% own two-thirds. What are the chances they would stand idly by while Congress and a president allowed a financial collapse, wiping out most or all of their net worth? The chances seem pretty slim from where I'm sitting.

The wealthy fought relentlessly for the big tax cuts of 2001, 2017 and 2025. But the money they made from those cuts would pale compared to the amount they'd lose in a crisis caused by a U.S. Treasury default. It's not even close. Ultimately they might even agree - eek! - to paying taxes like everyone else if that's the price of not getting wiped out. They know that 100% of nothing is nothing.

A stealth default by higher inflation looks like a likelier part of a long-term budget solution. Which, of course, would be good for TIPS as well.

-Brett Arends

data.title: NEW STUDY: WHITE MEMORIAL HOSPITALS GENERATE $1.2 BILLION IN ECONOMIC ACTIVITY AS L.A. HEALTHCARE SAFETY NET FACES GROWING PRESSURES
data.description:
NEW STUDY: WHITE MEMORIAL HOSPITALS GENERATE $1.2 BILLION IN ECONOMIC ACTIVITY AS L.A. HEALTHCARE SAFETY NET FACES GROWING PRESSURES

NEW STUDY: WHITE MEMORIAL HOSPITALS GENERATE $1.2 BILLION IN ECONOMIC ACTIVITY AS L.A. HEALTHCARE SAFETY NET FACES GROWING PRESSURES

PR Newswire

LOS ANGELES, Sept. 11, 2026

Hospitals support 5,500 jobs while serving communities facing significant health, economic and environmental disparities.

LOS ANGELES, Sept. 11, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- As hospitals serving high-need communities face growing financial pressures, a new study finds Adventist Health White Memorial and Adventist Health White Memorial Montebello generate more than $1.2 billion in annual economic activity and support approximately 5,500 jobs across Los Angeles County.

The study, conducted by the Los Angeles County Economic Development Corporation (LAEDC), examines the hospitals' roles as healthcare providers, employers, and community anchors. Together, they serve more than 2.4 million residents across their combined primary and secondary service areas.

"This study puts numbers behind something we see every day: Adventist Health White Memorial is deeply woven into the life of the communities we serve," said Daniel Fontoura, President of Adventist Health White Memorial and Adventist Health White Memorial Montebello. "Our impact begins with providing quality, compassionate healthcare, but reaches much further. Protecting this infrastructure is essential to the health and strength of our communities for generations to come."

The findings come at a critical time for the healthcare safety net. Approximately 86% of Adventist Health White Memorial's payor mix comes from Medi-Cal and Medicare, while the communities it serves already face significant barriers to healthcare. In its Primary Service Area, 14.4% of residents are uninsured, nearly twice the Los Angeles County average of 7.6%.

"Community hospitals such as Adventist Health White Memorial are an essential part of our healthcare safety net," said Paul Young, Senior Vice President of Advocacy and Public Policy at the Hospital Association of Southern California. "They provide trusted care close to home and help ensure that underserved communities are not left behind."

The hospitals' impact also extends throughout the regional economy through purchasing, employee spending, and support for local businesses.

"Adventist Health White Memorial Hospitals support thousands of jobs and generate economic activity that strengthens local businesses and benefits families throughout Los Angeles County," said Maria S. Salinas, President and CEO of the Los Angeles Area Chamber of Commerce. "Strong healthcare institutions help build strong communities, a thriving workforce and a more resilient regional economy."

Adventist Health White Memorial Foundation is calling on philanthropic partners, community leaders, and other stakeholders to help sustain healthcare access and community investment.

"Safeguarding our communities is a shared responsibility," said Juan De La Cruz, President of Adventist Health White Memorial Foundation Los Angeles & Montebello. "Together, we can protect access to care while building a stronger, more resilient region."

About Adventist Health White Memorial

Adventist Health White Memorial and Adventist Health White Memorial Montebello are nonprofit, faith-based hospitals providing compassionate, whole-person care across Los Angeles County. Together, the hospitals provide more than 545 licensed beds and offer inpatient, outpatient, emergency, diagnostic and specialty services.

About the Economic Impact Study

The study was conducted by the Los Angeles County Economic Development Corporation's Institute for Applied Economics and evaluates the hospitals' economic and fiscal impact, including direct operations, supply-chain activity, and employee spending, as well as conditions in the communities they serve.

Stephen Chavez, ChavezPR, (310) 486-4104, stephen@chavezpr.com

data.title: Robbins LLP Reminds Investors of the Pending September 21, 2026, Lead Plaintiff Deadline in the Securities Fraud Class Action Lawsuit Filed Against EQPT After a Significant Decline in the Company's Stock Price Following its IPO
data.description:
Robbins LLP Reminds Investors of the Pending September 21, 2026, Lead Plaintiff Deadline in the Securities Fraud Class Action Lawsuit Filed Against EQPT After a Significant Decline in the Company's Stock Price Following its IPO

Robbins LLP Reminds Investors of the Pending September 21, 2026, Lead Plaintiff Deadline in the Securities Fraud Class Action Lawsuit Filed Against EQPT After a Significant Decline in the Company's Stock Price Following its IPO

PR Newswire

SAN DIEGO, Sept. 11, 2026

SAN DIEGO, Sept. 11, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Robbins LLP reminds investors that a securities class action has been filed on behalf of shareholders who purchased or otherwise acquired EquipmentShare.com, Inc. (NASDAQ: EQPT): (1) Class A common stock issued in connection with the Company's January 2026 initial public offering ("IPO"), or (2) securities between January 23, 2026 and June 23, 2026, inclusive (the "Class Period"). EquipmentShare.com operates T3, an integrated cloud-based platform used for equipment rental and construction equipment management.

The lawsuit alleges that EquipmentShare.com, Inc. made false and misleading statements and omissions concerning undisclosed related-party transactions and its financial condition in connection with its IPO and during the Class Period.

Investors who purchased EQPT securities during the applicable period and suffered losses may have legal rights. Investors seeking appointment as lead plaintiff must file their papers with the court by September 21, 2026.

Listen to our podcast.

What Is the EquipmentShare.com Class Action About?

According to the complaint, EquipmentShare.com completed its IPO on January 26, 2026. The lawsuit alleges that EquipmentShare.com's IPO Registration Statement and subsequent statements during the Class Period failed to disclose material information concerning the Company's relationships and transactions with entities allegedly owned or controlled by its co-founders.

Specifically, plaintiff alleges that EquipmentShare.com failed to disclose that:

  1. the Company participated in additional undisclosed related-party transactions;
  2. the Company had not terminated or substantially reduced certain transactions with entities allegedly owned or controlled by its co-founders; and
  3. as a result, the Company's financial statements were materially misleading.

What Happened to EQPT Stock?

According to the complaint, on June 24, 2026, Umibōzu Research published a report containing allegations concerning EquipmentShare.com's related-party transactions. The report alleged that undisclosed related-party transactions had generated at least $77 million for entities affiliated with EquipmentShare.com's founders, with the report claiming the actual amount could be substantially higher.

The report also alleged that EquipmentShare.com maintained a high-net-worth individual and family-office channel involving entities identified as EZ Equipment Zone ("EZ"), Bevel Financial ("Bevel"), and Armada Fleet Management ("Armada"). According to the report, EquipmentShare.com's OWN program allegedly directed significant fees and other payments to related parties and involved a network of affiliated entities.

Following publication of the report, EquipmentShare.com stock fell $1.58 per share, or approximately 6.62%, to close at $22.30 on June 24, 2026. The stock continued to decline on June 25, 2026, falling another $2.61 per share, or approximately 11.7%, to close at $19.69.

By the time the lawsuit commenced, EQPT had traded as low as $16.06 per share, representing a decline of more than 34.5% from the Company's $24.50 IPO price.

Who May Be Eligible to Participate in the EquipmentShare.com Class Action?

Investors who (i) purchased EquipmentShare.com Class A common stock issued in connection with the January 2026 IPO; and/or (2) purchased or otherwise acquired EquipmentShare.com securities between January 23, 2026 and June 23, 2026 may be eligible to participate in the proposed securities class action. Investors who purchased EQPT securities during the applicable period and suffered losses may have rights under the federal securities laws.

What Is the EquipmentShare.com Lead Plaintiff Deadline?

The deadline for investors seeking appointment as lead plaintiff is September 21, 2026. The lead plaintiff is a representative investor who acts on behalf of other members of the proposed class in directing the litigation. Investors do not have to become lead plaintiff to potentially participate in any recovery obtained through the class action. Investors who choose to take no action may remain absent class members, subject to the rights and requirements applicable to the case.

Contact Robbins LLP

Investors seeking additional information about the EquipmentShare.com securities class action may submit an inquiry, email attorney Aaron Dumas, Jr., or give us a call at (800) 350-6003.

About Robbins LLP

A recognized leader in shareholder rights litigation, Robbins LLP has helped restore more than $1 billion in value to shareholders and secured some of the largest recoveries in shareholder derivative litigation history. 

"Behind everything we do is the belief that companies should be governed responsibly, fiduciaries should be held accountable, and shareholders deserve transparency and fairness," said Brian J. Robbins, Founding Partner of Robbins LLP.

To be notified if a class action against EquipmentShare.com, Inc settles or to receive free alerts when corporate executives engage in wrongdoing, sign up for Stock Watch today.
